qud-164.front: Which category of sunnah is a mustaḥabb action?

qud-165.front: Al-Qudūrī lists six actions of wuḍūʾ as mustaḥabb. What is the preferred position on his list?
qud-165.back: That it's an oversight: five of the six are really sunnah <bdi>مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>. Only wiping the neck is mustaḥabb.

qud-166.text: Wiping {{c2::the neck}} is the one action of wuḍūʾ that is only {{c1::mustaḥabb}}
qud-166.extra: Mustaḥabb is sunnah <bdi>غَيْر مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>: recommended and encouraged.

qud-167.text: These five actions of wuḍūʾ are each {{c6::a sunnah <bdi>مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>}} (numbers 10–14): {{c1::intending purification at the start}}; {{c2::wiping the whole head}}; {{c3::doing it in sequence}}; {{c4::beginning with the right}}; {{c5::doing it consecutively}}
qud-167.extra: Fourteen in total; 1–5 and 6–9 are on the companion cards. Al-Qudūrī's text lists these five as mustaḥabb, which the commentators count as an oversight.

qud-270.back: In tayammum it is obligatory; in wuḍūʾ it is a sunnah <bdi>مُؤَكَّدَة</bdi>, not a requirement — fittingly, <bdi>تَيَمُّم</bdi> itself means to intend
